issues: File `backend/app/main.py` line 1: `app` is used before it is defined, causing a NameError when the FastAPI application is imported. Define a FastAPI instance (e.g. `app = FastAPI()`) before any route decorators.

File `backend/app/main.py` is missing required imports: `FastAPI`, `Depends`, `Session` (from `sqlalchemy.orm`), `schemas`, `crud`, `get_db`, `create_access_token`, and any other utilities used in route definitions. Import these at the top of the file.

File `backend/app/main.py` only defines the `/auth/signup` endpoint; the `/auth/login` endpoint required by the acceptance tests is missing. Implement a POST `/auth/login` route that verifies credentials using `crud.authenticate_user` and returns a JWT token.

All other required endpoints are missing: POST `/receipts` (protected), GET `/receipts` (protected), POST `/mileage` (protected), GET `/mileage` (protected), GET `/dashboard` (protected), GET `/export/csv` (protected), GET `/export/pdf` (protected), and optionally GET `/media/{filename}`. Implement these routes according to the specification and the tests’ expectations.

The upload endpoints (`/receipts` and `/mileage`) must be protected with authentication. Add `Depends(get_current_user)` to the route signatures and ensure the JWT token is validated before processing requests.

File `backend/app/main.py` does not include CORS middleware. The app should add `CORSMiddleware` that reads allowed origins from the `FRONTEND_ORIGIN` environment variable (default to `http://localhost:19006`).

File `backend/app/main.py` does not set common security HTTP headers (e.g., `Strict-Transport-Security`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy`). Add a FastAPI middleware to inject these headers on all responses.

File `backend/app/auth.py` falls back to using the short `JWT_SECRET_KEY` value when the environment variable is present but shorter than 32 bytes, which is insecure. Instead, enforce a minimum 32‑byte secret: either raise an error if the provided secret is too short or always generate a secure random secret when the provided one is insufficient.

The Expo front‑end contains vulnerable transitive dependencies (`braces`, `node-forge`, `decode-uri-component`, `uuid`). Update `package.json` (or lockfile) to use fixed versions where available (e.g., upgrade `uuid` to `^13.0.0` or later, ensure `decode-uri-component` is at least `0.5.0` – already declared, but update the lockfile, and replace/remove any direct usage of `node-forge` if present). Re‑run `npm install` to regenerate `package-lock.json` without the vulnerable versions.

Frontend token storage on the web platform uses `AsyncStorage`, which is not secure against XSS. For production, replace the web storage fallback with httpOnly secure cookies or another browser‑secure storage mechanism. (If this is outside the scope of the acceptance tests, at least add a comment noting the limitation.)
feedback: The FastAPI application cannot be imported because `app` and related symbols are undefined, and many required routes are missing. Implement the missing imports, create the FastAPI instance, add all endpoints (including login, receipt/mileage CRUD, dashboard, and export), protect upload routes with JWT authentication, and configure CORS and security headers as described. Also address the insecure JWT secret handling and update the vulnerable npm dependencies. Once these changes are made, the acceptance tests should be able to import the app and exercise the full API flow.
